::: {.module-lead}
**Estimated time:** 5 minutes  
**Guiding question:** When does a research problem belong on Longleaf rather than a laptop?
:::

## Learning goals

By the end of this module, participants should be able to:

- describe Longleaf in plain language;
- identify research tasks that benefit from shared computing resources; and
- explain where Longleaf fits between a personal computer and a cloud service.

## Why researchers outgrow laptops

Frame Longleaf around familiar research constraints: analyses that take too long, datasets that exceed local memory, repeated models that can run independently, or work that must continue after a laptop is disconnected.

<!-- Add one audience-relevant research example and a simple laptop-versus-cluster comparison. -->

## What Longleaf is

Introduce Longleaf as a shared computing cluster: many computers coordinated so researchers can request the processing time, memory, and software needed for a particular job.

## A brief history and context

<!-- Add a short, verified Longleaf history and its role within UNC Research Computing. -->

## Key takeaway

Longleaf is not simply a faster personal computer. It is a shared system where work is described as a job, assigned resources, and scheduled to run on an appropriate compute node.
